key_insight: EHR-Complex is a large-scale benchmark for interactive, multi-step clinical reasoning over real EHR data, revealing that current medical agents still struggle with complex database tasks.
clinical_relevance: It better reflects how clinicians and health systems might query longitudinal patient records and population data than static SQL benchmarks, making it useful for testing practical EHR agents.
method: Built on MIMIC-IV with 365K patients, 31 tables, and 500M+ records.
Defines ~52K tasks across six clinical intents at both patient and population levels.
Requires agents to interact via SQL or Python in a sandboxed environment.
evidence_signal: Across evaluation, the top model reached only 62.3% exact-match accuracy, and pass@k consistency dropped below 50% for nearly all models at k=4.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to SQL generation errors, code execution behavior, and medical-code lookup quality, so benchmark results may not translate directly to real-world deployment.
paper_title: EHR-Complex: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Complex Clinical Reasoning
